s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unilateral skin hardening with limited joint motion
salient_findings: Unilateral skin hardening on the right thigh and buttock
Limited motion of the right limb joint
key_facts: Stony-hard plaque on the right thigh and buttock
Normal autoantibodies, immunoglobulins, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
MRI showed slight thickening of subcutaneous tissue and T2 signal abnormality
Histopathological findings: normal epidermis, mild pigmentation, increased density of fibroblasts, and adipocyte entrapment
Increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive unilateral skin hardening with limited joint motion
salient_findings: Unilateral skin hardening on the right thigh and buttock
Limited motion of the right limb joint
key_facts: Stony-hard plaque on the right thigh and buttock
Normal autoantibodies, immunoglobulins, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate

Increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis

shortlist.label: Linear Scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of progressive unilateral skin hardening and limited joint motion

shortlist.label: Morphea
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by stony-hard plaques and loss of skin elasticity, consistent with the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely than linear scleroderma, still a plausible diagnosis given the skin hardening and joint limitation

shortlist.label: Lipedematous Sclerosing Panniculitis
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's histopathological findings of increased density of fibroblasts and adipocyte entrapment are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Scleroedema Adultorum
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms of skin hardening and limited joint motion, combined with the lack of inflammation on histopathology, make this a possible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of progressive unilateral skin hardening on the right thigh and buttock, along with loss of skin elasticity and mild hypertrichosis, is consistent with Linear Scleroderma. The disease's typical age of onset and the absence of systemic symptoms or abnormal laboratory tests also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Morphea
rejected.why: Morphea typically presents with well-defined, circular plaques, which is not consistent with the patient's ill-defined, stony-hard plaque.

rejected.label: Scleroderma
rejected.why: Scleroderma is a systemic disease that often presents with autoantibodies and abnormal laboratory tests, which are not present in this patient.

rejected.label: Lipedematous Sclerosing Panniculitis
rejected.why: Lipedematous Sclerosing Panniculitis is a rare condition that typically presents with painful, indurated lesions, which is not consistent with the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Scleroedema Adultorum
rejected.why: Scleroedema Adultorum is a condition that typically presents with sudden onset of skin induration, often associated with diabetes or other systemic diseases, which is not consistent with the patient's 7-year duration of symptoms and lack of underlying medical conditions.
